record.paper_title: On free curves and related open problems
record.context_brief: Relation between ct plus st and ν
record.original_question: For a reduced plane curve C:f=0 in P^2, what general relationship exists between the sum ct(f)+st(f) of the coincidence and stability thresholds of the Jacobian algebra and the freeness-defect invariant ν(C)=max_j dim N(f)_j? The paper notes a formula for plus-one generated curves but says no general linear dependence can hold even for all 3-syzygy curves.

evidence.quote: The relation between this invariant ct(f) + st(f) and the defect of freeness ν(C) is also an open problem.
However, the formulas in (6.2) below show that such a linear dependence cannot hold in general, even for 3-syzygy curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C: f=0$ be a reduced plane curve in $\mathbb{P}^2$ defined by a homogeneous polynomial $f \in S = \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ of degree $d$. Let $J_f = (\partial_x f, \partial_y f, \partial_z f)$ be the Jacobian ideal and let $M(f) = S/J_f$ be the Jacobian (Milnor) algebra, which is a graded $S$-module. Let $I_f$ denote the saturation of $J_f$ with respect to the irrelevant ideal $(x,y,z)$, and let $N(f) = I_f / J_f$, which is a finite-dimensional graded $\mathbb{C}$-vector space.

Define the following invariants:
\begin{itemize}
\item The coincidence threshold $\mathrm{ct}(f) = \max\{q \;:\; \dim M(f)_k = \dim M(f_s)_k \text{ for all } k \le q\}$, where $f_s$ is a smooth homogeneous polynomial of degree $d$ in $S$.
\item The stability threshold $\mathrm{st}(f) = \min\{q \;:\; \dim M(f)_k = \tau(C) \text{ for all } k \ge q\}$, where $\tau(C) = \dim M(f)_{3(d-2)}$ is the global Tjurina number of $C$.
\item The freeness defect $\nu(C) = \max_j \dim N(f)_j$.
\end{itemize}

Determine the general relationship between $\mathrm{ct}(f) + \mathrm{st}(f)$ and $\nu(C)$ valid for every reduced plane curve $C \subset \mathbb{P}^2$. In particular, although a closed formula relating these quantities is known for plus-one generated curves, no linear relation between $\mathrm{ct}(f)+\mathrm{st}(f)$ and $\nu(C)$ can hold for all 3-syzygy curves; find what general (possibly nonlinear) bound or identity does hold.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly stated as open in the survey on free curves and related open problems. A subsequent 2025 preprint "Some remarks on plane curves related to freeness" and related recent work (2024-2025) discusses these thresholds but does not provide a general formula relating ct(f)+st(f) to ν(C); the absence of a linear relation even for 3-syzygy curves is reiterated. No solution was found.

status_evidence.snippet: The relation between this invariant ct(f) + st(f) and the defect of freeness ν(C) is also an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The author explicitly states the relationship is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Some remarks on plane curves related to freeness
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work investigating thresholds and freeness defects of plane curves; no general relation between ct+st and ν is established.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work does not resolve the general relation.
